analysis:
The PR changes only docs/reference/configuration.md. The visible patch adds one row (head line 414 per the file_changes range) documenting DARKBLOOM_TTFT_GDN_BLOCKED. This is a Gated DeltaNet prompt-window kernel selector for qwen3_5 models. The default is a probe that keeps a four-row kernel only where it reproduces gated_delta_step bit for bit; `0`/`false`/`no`/`off` roll back to the stock kernel; `packed` or `rows` force a kernel without the check. The row says it is forwarded to the LaunchAgent. Neither supplied unit contains line 414: unit 4 is base text from 519 on, and unit 5 is head text from line 1 and appears truncated before line 414. I could therefore not verify the row's exact text, only the patch excerpt, which is itself truncated.

Security relevance: this is a documentation-only change, so no code, authorization, attestation or encryption controls changed here. The documented behavior touches the TB-007 inference engine and could affect output integrity (T-007, T-027 by analogy). The row claims bit-exact equivalence is checked by default, and says forced kernels skip the check and are for A/B measurement only. Because the variable is forwarded to the LaunchAgent, an operator-set force value would persist in a serving daemon. The operator is already the adversary in ADV-001/T-007, and the threat model already treats the provider as able to serve manipulated outputs, so this adds no new trust-boundary exposure.

The unchanged context I examined (prefix cache SSD settings, T-041 related config, App Attest worker flags, endpoint resumption and logout) is consistent with the existing threat model. Nothing in it conflicts with the T-041 TTL, HMAC lookup or storage posture.

Remaining questions for integration: (1) whether the kernel code in GatedDelta.swift actually matches the documented bit-exact probe and rollback semantics; (2) whether forwarding to the LaunchAgent is implemented in LaunchAgent.passthroughEnvKeys. Neither is in the supplied evidence, so I record them as unverified contracts rather than findings.
